tests.display_text: Imagine walking through two streets on a hot afternoon. One has a line of trees. The other has buildings and concrete, but almost no shade. The second street may feel much hotter. Why? Trees stop some sunlight from reaching the ground. Water evaporating from their leaves may also affect the air around them. But planting any tree anywhere is not a guaranteed fix. The species, its size, the water it gets, and the direction of the street all matter. Shade moves as the sun moves too. So, if we want to understand heat in a city, one photograph or one reading will not tell us enough. We need measurements at different times, and we need to compare places with and without trees. The next time you step into a shady street, notice the relief. There is a small natural system working above your head.
